owner_directive: 2026-11-07 — when boards are stuck, lanes must know which agent resolves it, and reversible blockers (release cut, dirty branch, stale lock) are resolved by the fleet, never queued behind a human. Waiting for a human is the worst possible option.
rule: reversible => resolve now, with the command named here. Irreversible => escalate to the owner with the measured condition and the default action you will take if no answer arrives.

classes.symptom: git mutation dies: 'could not write index' / 'stash failed', or a lock nobody explains
classes.resolver: the lane that owns the tick
commands: fuser -v .git/index.lock
ps -o pid,stat,etime,args -p <PID>
rm .git/index.lock   # ONLY when the holder is a READER (status/ls-files) and D-state for minutes
classes.escalate_when: the holder is a MUTATING command (commit/merge/rebase) — kill or wait for that holder instead of removing the lock

classes.symptom: worktree dirty with paths the tick did not write
classes.resolver: foreman (attribute), then the lane that owns the producer
commands: git status --porcelain
git diff --cached --text
git checkout HEAD -- .gitreins/tasks.yaml   # harness state only, after a quiet process census
classes.escalate_when: the paths are a live sibling's real edits (modified tracked files with fresh mtimes and an owning process) — never adopt or discard those

commands: git fetch origin
git rebase origin/main
git push origin main
git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main   # must equal git rev-parse HEAD
classes.escalate_when: never for a landable divergence; only when the push target itself is being retargeted by policy

classes.symptom: guard FAIL whose finding was already true at the base commit
classes.signature: run the same gate on `origin/main` or on the pre-fix tree; identical finding = pre-existing
commands: git stash --include-untracked && <gate> ; git stash pop   # prove the finding exists without your diff
git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit   # only with the pre-existing proof quoted in the message
classes.escalate_when: the gate fails identically on a CLEAN checkout of origin/main and blocks every lane — then the gate itself is the defect and gets a row

commands: gitreins judge --status <job-id>
cat .gitreins/history/<date>/<id>/verdict.json
# fix the cited criterion, then rerun the judge SEQUENTIALLY (never two judges in one checkout)
classes.escalate_when: the verdict cites an acceptance criterion that cannot be satisfied without an owner decision — then the ROW is the escalation, not the judge

classes.resolver: merge-reconciler pattern (third-party resolution) or the foreman
commands: git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD   # clean tree hash = merge is mechanical
# resolve, then re-run the repo's gates on the MERGED tree before committing
classes.escalate_when: both sides changed the same semantic contract and neither side's tests express the intended behaviour

classes.signature: scheduler shows the lane enabled with no tick in N cycles; cooldown pin in config
commands: curl -s localhost:9090/api/v1/projects/<lane> | jq '.enabled,.cooldown,.admission_mode'
# fix the pin (fleet.toml AND DB outrank the router), then force one tick and verify the tick row
classes.escalate_when: the fix needs a spend or policy decision (raising max_concurrent above the load gate)

classes.symptom: model/provider refusal (402, 429, circuit open, wrong seat served)
classes.signature: circuit state + post-dispatch `session_model_usage` (labels lie; the seat is what was billed)
commands: router circuit clear --all
# dispatch, then verify the SERVED model in state.db session_model_usage, not the requested label
classes.escalate_when: the account itself is exhausted or a provider account must be added (spend/credentials)

classes.signature: dispatch resolves to a fallback or errors 'model not found'; pin predates the current generation
commands: grep -n '<model-id>' fleet.toml   # fix BOTH the project pin and the DB row
# re-dispatch and verify the served model
classes.escalate_when: the replacement changes the cost tier the owner chose

classes.symptom: row blocked on a row that is already complete
classes.signature: the referenced id's status in the board
commands: boardctl show <blocker-id> --json
boardctl update <id> --status pending --note 'blocker <id> complete; prerequisite re-probed live at <ts>'
# or REPLACE the blocker with the newly measured gate when the prerequisite is still dead
classes.escalate_when: never — a satisfied pointer is bookkeeping, and a dead prerequisite is a new measurement

classes.symptom: environment down: service, container or host
classes.signature: `docker inspect` (restart policy + exit code + finished_at) or `systemctl --user show <u> -p ActiveEnterTimestamp,ExecMainStatus`
classes.resolver: foreman, on a host it can reach
commands: docker inspect <c> --format 'restart={{.HostConfig.RestartPolicy.Name}} exitcode={{.State.ExitCode}}'
systemctl --user show <u> -p ActiveEnterTimestamp,ExecMainStatus
# a clean exit under restart=unless-stopped, or an inactive unit with no failure, is STOPPABLE: restore it and re-run the row's original arms
classes.escalate_when: the component is genuinely retired (renamed/migrated/replaced) — then re-scope the row instead of escalating

classes.symptom: duplicate rows / reused ids inflating the board
classes.signature: same content fingerprint under two ids; `dedupe-board --dry-run`
commands: dedupe-board --dry-run
# keep the row carrying evidence, close the twin with a note naming the survivor
classes.escalate_when: never — duplicates are provable by fingerprint

classes.signature: release readiness gates green on the exact commit; tag absent
commands: # cut the tag on the verified commit; a tag is reversible until it is published to consumers
git tag -a v<X.Y.Z> <sha> && git push origin v<X.Y.Z>
classes.escalate_when: the release contains a breaking change or a version policy decision — not for a routine tagged build

classes.symptom: IRREVERSIBLE: deletion of live data, secrets/credentials, spend, policy change, doctrine conflict
classes.signature: the action cannot be undone by a later commit (data gone, money spent, tag protection changed, two owner rulings conflict)
classes.escalate_when: always — escalate once, naming the exact question, the options, and the default you will take if no answer arrives; a repeat ask is a signal the escalation path is broken
